items.headline: Yemen: Houthis report deadly Saudi strikes on Taiz market
items.snippet: The Houthi-run health ministry accused the Saudi Air Force of committing an "abominable crime," vowing to retaliate. The Houthis' account of the attack cannot be independently verified.

items.headline: Avalanche in Nepal leaves 2 dead, several missing
items.snippet: An avalanche has struck the Himlung Himal base camp in Nepal after days of severe weather. Two guides are confirmed dead and at least 14 people remain missing in the remote region.

items.headline: UK: 5 arrested after 'major incident' near Fairford air base
items.snippet: Scores of homes were evacuated in the UK town of Whelford, near an air base used by the US military, with bomb disposal teams checking "suspicious vehicles" at the scene. Police said five men had been arrested.

items.headline: Two people killed as bus crashes on way to Oktoberfest
items.snippet: The bus was traveling from Italy to Munich, carrying 33 Filipino tourists who wanted to visit the famous beer festival. One of the dozens injured remains in life-threatening condition.

items.headline: Pope decries 'scourge' of sexual abuse during France visit
items.snippet: French bishops took "courageous" steps when faced with "the painful scourge of abuse of minors," Pope Leo XIV told the high-ranking clerics before his scheduled meeting with survivors at the Catholic shrine of Lourdes.

items.headline: European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
items.snippet: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

items.headline: Switzerland: Voters reject stricter view of neutrality
items.snippet: Early projections show Swiss voters rejecting a stricter application of the country's vaunted neutrality. Swiss neutrality has been enshrined in the constitution since 1848.

items.headline: Germany news: Are Germans giving up their beloved meat and sausages?
items.snippet: Germans used to be all about sausages and meat. While those do remain popular, things seem to be slowly changing. There also are new insights into the economic side of East Germany's espionage DW has more.

items.headline: Northern Ireland: Pro-UK march to go through Catholic area
items.snippet: It's the first time the march has been allowed to go through the area since 1997. Overnight, a court ruling allowed it to take place after a series of last-minute legal challenges that reached Belfast's High Court.

items.headline: India news: Kolkata's SRFTI students allege violent attack
items.snippet: Students at Kolkata's Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute say they were attacked with knives after confronting an outside group over a meeting they allege was affiliated with the right-wing Hindu RSS.

items.headline: Iran sticks to Hormuz plan after Trump rejects it
items.snippet: Iranian officials that while they were aware of Trump's comments on rejecting the new proposal, they had not received a formal message rejecting the plan that would open the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: No public mentions of Taiwan at official Xi and Trump meeting
items.snippet: At a high-profile summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington, there was much talk of trade and artificial intelligence. One of the most contentious issues, Taiwan, was only discussed in private.

items.headline: China sends two giant pandas off to Atlanta zoo after Xi-Trump summit
items.snippet: Ping Ping and Fu Shuang took off to Atlanta on a FedEx plane, with steamed corn buns, carrots and bamboo to snack on during the flight. Their trip is one of the few concrete things to come out the Xi-Trump summit.

items.headline: Gunmen kill 27 people in two mass shootings in South Africa
items.snippet: South African police have launched a search for suspects after 17 people were found dead at a tavern southwest of Johannesburg. A separate tavern shooting near Cape Town left 10 dead.

items.headline: Why farmers are pairing crops with solar panels
items.snippet: From cooler soil to paid grazing land, farmers in the US are finding that solar panels can do more than generate power.

items.headline: Powerful storm batters northeast US, hundreds of flights canceled
items.snippet: Hundreds of flights were canceled and thousands were delayed as a nor'easter brought flooding, power cuts and travel disruption to cities like New York, Boston and Philadelphia.

items.headline: Spain: Thousands protest in Madrid against housing crisis
items.snippet: Tens of thousands rallied in the Spanish capital after an 87-year-old woman was dramatically evicted from her home this week. Protesters called for measures to curb rising costs and reduce evictions.

items.headline: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
items.snippet: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

items.headline: China, US agree to set up channel for AI safety incidents
items.snippet: Following the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the two superpowers pledged to set up a "communication channel" for AI incidents and boost coordination on military matters.

items.headline: Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
items.snippet: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

items.headline: Russian students: Propaganda in school prepares them to die
items.snippet: The Russian government wants children to learn about patriotism from an early age. DW spoke to students in Siberia about their views on propaganda at school on the war in Ukraine and their future.

items.headline: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
items.snippet: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

items.headline: 'Lithuanian skies are NATO skies': DW speaks with Lithuanian premier Mindaugas Sinkevicius
items.snippet: In a DW interview, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius discussed threats to Lithuania from Russia and Belarus, NATO's need for stronger air defense and why military spending alone cannot ensure security.

items.headline: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
items.snippet: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.

items.headline: How Bulgaria become a global leader in battery storage and what this means for the country's grid and energy market?
items.snippet: In under two years, Bulgaria has become one of the world's most battery-intensive energy markets. Can the surge last — and what will it mean for conventional power generators?

items.headline: Italy to ban burqa in schools, limit foreign pupils
items.snippet: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has passed new school rules capping the number of students who don't speak fluent Italian and banning face coverings.

items.headline: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
items.snippet: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.

items.headline: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
items.snippet: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.

items.headline: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
items.snippet: Germany's economy is growing again, but recovery remains on shaky ground. High government spending is keeping the economy afloat, while energy prices, a shortage of skilled workers and debt continue to weigh on it.

items.headline: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
items.snippet: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.

items.headline: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
items.snippet: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.

items.headline: Germany news: Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid
items.snippet: Berlin's decision to withdraw its Olympic bid means that only Munich and the western Rhine/Ruhr region are left in the running as potential Olympic hosts. DW has more.

items.headline: Czech PM Andrej Babis reiterates importance of NATO for his country but rejects calls to increase defense spending
items.snippet: The US and NATO want Czechia to spend more on defense. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis says Prague cannot afford faster increases, despite growing warnings about the threat from Russia.

items.headline: 'Pope fever' takes hold as Pope Leo visits France
items.snippet: Pope Leo XIV is expected to draw huge crowds during his visit to France. As part of his trip, he's also set to address Europe's future and some of the challenges ahead.

items.headline: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
items.snippet: The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?

items.headline: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
items.snippet: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

items.headline: Slovakia: PM Robert Fico's NATO Article 5 remarks spark criticism and raise questions about his country's NATO commitment
items.snippet: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says he fears war and will do everything he can to keep his country out of one. Critics say his remarks risk weakening NATO, the alliance that was designed to prevent such a war.

items.headline: Germany's oldest party, the center-left SPD, is in a difficult position following its success in the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state election
items.snippet: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) has vowed to press ahead with controversial reforms, but resistance is mounting within his coalition partner, the SPD. How much dissent can a governing coalition tolerate?

items.headline: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
items.snippet: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.

items.headline: Famine threatens the Ukrainian town of Oleshky in the southern Kherson region as Russia delays creating a humanitarian evacuation corridor

items.snippet: A memoir penned by Charles Spencer on his older sister's life has been released, opening old royal wounds nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death.

items.snippet: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?
